headline: Ohio governor: a poll and an ad on the same day

That afternoon a video featuring Acton's estranged mother calling her a liar spread on social media, and at about 3:30 pm the Ramaswamy campaign said it made the ad and would spend 4 million dollars promoting it (retrieved, NBC News). Republicans including Meghan McCain and a DeWine appointee condemned it, and Sherrod Brown called it disgusting (retrieved, Newsweek). Kalshi's price for Acton went from 72 at 9 am to 74 by 11 am and 77 by 5 pm; Polymarket closed at 78.5 from 72.5 (retrieved, hourly prices). The day before, ActiVote had Ramaswamy up 2.8 among 400 likely voters (retrieved, polls feed). The event feed's first pull had not reached the governor's race at writing time, but the Ohio Senate feed carried the ad coverage: 8 ad and 8 scandal articles in 48 hours.
why_it_moved: About two points on the poll by late morning and about three more on the ad in the afternoon, by the timing of the price path (inferred). The poll is the measured part. The ad is a reaction, not a measurement.
should_it_move_us: Wait. The poll alone moves a seven-poll average by about a point, and our 63 already carries a 2 to 2.5 point Ohio polling-bias assumption against Democrats. The ad has no poll behind it yet.

headline: Ohio governor: every benchmark moves toward Acton, no post-ad poll
what_happened: Retrieved. Fox News (Beacon Research and Shaw and Co.) fielded Oct 15 to 19, released Oct 21 at 6 pm: Acton 50, Ramaswamy 48 among 1,592 likely voters, Acton +4 among 2,005 registered. Fox says the survey closed before the ad became public. ActiVote, Sep 27 to Oct 19, 400 likely voters: Ramaswamy 51, Acton 49. Sabato's Crystal Ball on Oct 22 moved the race from Toss-up to Leans Democratic, citing the Silver Bulletin average of Acton +4.7 and the ad, and warning that Ohio polls understated Republicans in 2018. Our ratings pull shows Silver Bulletin at Likely Democratic from Lean; the page is paywalled and says updated Oct 20. Decision Desk went to 70 from 50 in our pull; a direct check of its page returned HTTP 429. Polymarket 77.5 to 83.5 and Kalshi 76.5 to 82.5 since the Oct 21 evening pull, and +5 from midnight to 20:10 today. The ad features Acton's estranged mother. Secretary of State LaRose distanced himself Oct 21, Trump said Oct 21 it was not Ramaswamy's doing then praised it Oct 22 on Truth Social, and Governor DeWine on Oct 22 called it deeply troubling and asked that it come down. Ohio's Secretary of State dashboard, coded by last primary ballot taken (Ohio has no party registration): of 828,847 ballots received, 33.3 percent Democratic primary voters and 27.4 percent Republican, against 17.4 and 27.4 at the end of 2024.
why_it_moved: Inferred. The ad backlash crossing into the Republican party, with DeWine and Trump on opposite sides, is the market driver, since no poll fielded after the ad exists. The Fox poll confirms an Acton lead but a smaller one than Marist's 8. The ratings and Decision Desk follow the average and the ad story, and Decision Desk blends the market at 25 percent, so part of its 20 points is the price. The primary-ballot early-vote split cannot be read as a party split: Democrats had the contested 2026 primary.
should_it_move_us: Wait. Our core number is 70 (margin Acton +3.8) and the run's judgment is 63. The model counted ActiVote at Ramaswamy +2 and left the Fox poll out under its partisan (D/R) rule for the Beacon and Shaw pair, which is a classification to check, not a reason to move. Both new polls are below the average and both predate the ad, so today's moves are narrative and market-blended, not new polling.

headline: Blanche will not rule out a DOJ role in certification
what_happened: Not flagged by the scripts, added here. Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters in Norfolk, Virginia on 2026-10-22 that there could be a doomsday scenario in which the Justice Department would seek to get involved in certification, that it is not DOJ's intention to improperly interfere with elections or the state certification process, and that he is not planning his days around the election to be somewhere to not certify (retrieved, NBC News). why_it_moved: Nothing moved in the gate items. This is a statement of posture, not an action. It belongs to the gate agent's record because it is the first time the sitting attorney general has declined to rule out DOJ involvement in state certification this cycle.
should_it_move_us: Wait. The base rate is zero: the federal Justice Department has never blocked or delayed a state's certification of a federal election. A refusal to rule something out does not change a zero base rate. The gate agent should log it at its current severity and re-grade only on a filing.
